Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Participate(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenshipUS(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenshipTaiwan(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
Official(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
Manager(x, y) ::: x is a manager at y.
HoldTaiwaneseCitizenship(x) ::: x holds Taiwanese citizenship.
Vladimir(x) ::: x is Vladimir.
Ekaterina(x) ::: x is Ekaterina.
RegisterUS(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
ManageGazprom(x) ::: x is a manager at Gazprom.
Premises:
∀x (CanRegister(x) → Participate(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the 2024 US presidential election.
∀x (CitizenshipUS(x) → CanRegister(x)) ::: If someone has US citizenship, then they can register to vote.
∀x (CitizenshipUS(x) ∨ CitizenshipTaiwan(x)) ::: A person either has US citizenship or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬∃x (Official(x) ∧ CitizenshipTaiwan(x)) ::: No Russian Federation officials hold Taiwanese citizenship.
Vladimir(x) ∧ ¬CitizenshipTaiwan(x) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
Ekaterina(x) ::: Ekaterina.
RegisterUS(x) ∨ ManageGazprom(x) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote in the US or she is a manager at Gazprom.
Conclusion:
RegisterUS(Ekaterina) ∨ ManageGazprom(Ekaterina)
